ladder.teaches: range sum in O(1) from a prefix array
ladder.why: The base case with no story: build pre once, then every inclusive range [l, r] is pre[r+1] - pre[l].

ladder.teaches: range sum in O(1) from a prefix array
ladder.why: With a running prefix and the total, the left and right sums of every index are O(1), so one pass finds the balance point.

ladder.teaches: prefix sum + hash map to count subarrays with sum k
ladder.why: A subarray ending here sums to k when an earlier prefix equals current - k, so count earlier prefixes in a hash map; negatives are why a window fails.

ladder.teaches: prefix of a parity, a mod or a balance
ladder.why: Divisible by k means two prefixes with the same remainder, so the hash map counts remainders instead of sums.
A range add is +u at start and -u after end; one prefix sum over the difference array gives every slot's total.

ladder.teaches: prefix and suffix arrays (product except self, best left and right)
ladder.why: Everything except i is everything left of i times everything right of i: one prefix pass and one suffix pass, no division.
Each output cell is a clipped rectangle sum, answered in O(1) from a 2-D prefix table by inclusion-exclusion.

ladder.teaches: prefix of a parity, a mod or a balance
ladder.why: Amazon OA: score the two roles +1 and -1 so 'equal counts' becomes equal prefix balances, and keep the smallest skill prefix per balance.
Amazon OA: each user is a range +1 over days, so a difference array and one prefix sum give daily traffic.

ladder.teaches: prefix and suffix arrays (product except self, best left and right)
ladder.why: Amazon OA: the value of a day is max(prefix sum, suffix sum), so the answer is the best of two running-sum scans.

ladder.teaches: prefix sum + hash map to count subarrays with sum k
ladder.why: The prefix + hash map count with XOR in place of addition, since XOR undoes itself.

ladder.teaches: range sum in O(1) from a prefix array
ladder.why: A rhombus is a stack of row segments, so row prefix sums turn each segment into one subtraction.
2-D prefix sums make every k x k square O(1), and positive values make the valid k monotone so k can be searched.

ladder.teaches: prefix of a parity, a mod or a balance
ladder.why: Amazon OA: remainder equals length forces length < k and turns into equal keys (P[i] - i) mod k, counted in a hash map over a sliding range of prefixes.

notes: No clean 'Contiguous Array' (equal 0s and 1s) exists; amazon-get-max-skill-sum teaches the balance idea in an OA story instead, and ibm-longest-balanced-binary-subarray adds a prefix constraint that makes it a stack problem. amazon-num-of-suitable-places was left out: it is mainly a binary-search problem. The parity technique is covered by mod (inmobi divisible-by-k) and XOR; atlassian-beautiful-subarrays (prefix parity) went to sliding-window.
